nodes.name: Run bot-exec.sh on host
nodes.notes: Attach a DEDICATED SSH credential. See the bridge sticky note.

parameters.content:
## Telegram management bot  (locked to the operator)

Lets the operator monitor & control the platform from Telegram. **No AI** — every
command is deterministic. Flow:

```
Telegram Trigger → Authorize, parse & plan → Execute on host? ─┬─(true)→ Run bot-exec.sh (SSH) → Reply: command result
   (your bot)        (allowlist + whitelist)                   └─(false)→ Reply: message  (denial / help / unknown / error)
```

### One-time MANUAL setup (deferred — do this on the Pi)
1. **BotFather** → create a bot → copy the **token**.
2. Find **your** numeric Telegram user id (e.g. message `@userinfobot`).
3. In `.env`: set `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_IDS=<your id>` (comma-separated for more than
   one). Restart n8n so `$env.TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_IDS` is visible here.
4. In n8n, create a **Telegram API** credential (the BotFather token) and select
   it on **Telegram Trigger** and both **Reply** nodes.
5. Wire the host bridge (see the other note), then **Save** + toggle **Active**.

### SECURITY MODEL
- **Allowlist (fail closed):** the *Authorize* node only proceeds for a sender id
  in `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_IDS`. Empty id or empty allowlist → **denied**. Never an
  open bot.
- **Whitelist only:** unknown commands are refused with `/help`.
- **No secrets in replies.** The token lives in an n8n credential; the allowlist
  in `.env`. This JSON is committed — keep secrets OUT of it.

## The execution bridge — `scripts/bot-exec.sh`  (security boundary)

n8n is **not** given the Docker socket or the host filesystem. State/▸read
commands run on the host through **`scripts/bot-exec.sh`** over SSH with a
**dedicated key**. That script accepts ONLY a fixed action set, validates every
argument, logs every call, and never evals input.

### Wire the **Run bot-exec.sh on host** (SSH) node
1. Create a dedicated key on the Pi for n8n; add it as an n8n **SSH** credential
   (private key) and select it on the SSH node.
2. **Recommended hardening** — pin that key in `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` so it can
   ONLY launch the bridge (the requested action arrives in `$SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`):

   ```
   command="bash /PATH/TO/pi-system/scripts/bot-exec.sh --from-ssh",no-pty,no-port-forwarding,no-X11-forwarding,no-agent-forwarding ssh-ed25519 AAAA... n8n-bot
   ```
3. The SSH node sends only the **validated** `"<action> <arg>"` string; the host
   re-validates. Defence in depth.

Read-only: `/status /health /check /projects`. State-changing (logged):
`/up /down /project_up /project_down /audit_url /panel_audit_url`. The audit_url
family takes a SINGLE http(s) URL (no whitespace) and runs the same SSRF-guarded
SEO engine — `/audit_url` at standard depth, `/panel_audit_url` at deep depth
(specialist panel). The URL is rejected BEFORE Docker if it points at an internal
host / uses a non-http(s) scheme / embeds credentials; it is then passed as a
SINGLE argv element end-to-end (never interpolated). Full details: `docs/README.md`
→ *Telegram management bot*.
